answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ—both metrics that memory_86 and memory_31 directly addressed with positive results. Memory_86 showed that shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value; memory_31 showed that signup simplification (cutting required fields) produced durable first-week activation lift in SMBs. These are the highest-confidence levers available. Promotional pricing (memory_73) risks retention degradation and doesn't address the core engagement problem. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for existing customers but don't solve competitor acquisition pressure or activation decline. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address the SMB squeeze. Activation messaging (memory_91) has secondary evidence of impact. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding targets the measurable decline directly, replicates known success conditions, and preserves the option to layer activation messaging or referral incentives afterward if needed. This approach maximizes sustainable qualified revenue by improving product-market engagement rather than chasing price competition.
